title: Send-off
subtitle: They remembered an ancient verse, with whose meaning is lost to history.

trails.title: Lost to History
trails.description: What once represented new beginnings now only heralds an end.

content.text:
Dieterich Becker ​died from shelling on 1916/4/27.
Baethke Zimmermann ​died from shelling on 1916/4/27.
Simon Miller was reported missing on 1916/6/11, then was confirmed dead.
Miller's tag has been found.
Friedrich Bauer​ died from machine-gun fire on 1916/8/12.
...
Finn Wagner died from infection on 1916/11/7.
Elvin Neumann died of trench fever on 1916/11/8.
Felix Zimmermann ​died from shelling on 1916/12/8.
Julian Kruger ​died from infection after being shot on 1916/12/13.
Ben Becker died on 1916/12/14. Cause unclear.
...
Walter Schmidt died from shelling on 1918/1/12.
Paul Haumann died on 1918/3/11.
...
Eberhard Braun died on 1920/11/10.

items.text: Send-off
Graveyard

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Here you are, Eberhard.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Paul, it's good to see you, my friend. How's everyone holding up on the front?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: They are celebrating this war's end, singing songs and drinking beer. It's peaceful.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Hm. Peaceful.
He repeats the words with satisfaction. Eberhard's spirit has changed significantly from the last time they met.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: It's unexpected that the Foundation would allow you to move so freely.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Heh. No, my duty is done. I have no place in Montpaix—no place among suits and politics.
He exhales, stretching in the crisp morning air.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That red-haired official agreed to let me go for a walk every once in a while. He said, "Someone will keep an eye on you." Hah, whatever.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: It's getting cold, but I enjoy a crisp winter morning like this. It reminds me of our days as students.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Remember? We had to get up before dawn. I was lazier than you. I wouldn't wake up until you rode your bicycle to my window and shouted my name.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Then, the two of us would miss Latin class. Just as Walter did.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Hahaha, I don't blame him. Latin class was hell.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Walter. He was a good lad.
Paul removes a crumpled envelope from inside his jacket.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: This parcel is to be delivered to you. There's a letter within it from Mr. Mühlenberge, addressed to those of us in Class 3.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Mr. Mühlenberge ... I was planning to visit him during my home leave, but, well, you know what happened back home.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: But he doesn't have a clue about what happened out here. What use is this letter? You and I are the only two class members left since the fall of Montpaix.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: *sigh* Alright, let's hear it, Paul.
Steadying his breath, Paul tears it open.
He unfolds the letter.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "My dear students and honorable soldiers! The war has reached a critical point, and, as your teacher, it is my duty to boost your morale."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "I am aware that the vision of the war from the front lines may be more limited than for those of us in the fatherland. So, allow me to make things clear: victory is within our grasp."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "Though I'm certain life on the front is tough, remember, this is a sacrifice for a greater cause. Therefore, let your suffering be sweet!"

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "... This will be the most glorious moment of your lives. And, as I have taught you, perhaps it will please us one day to remember these things."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: "Please us"? Ha. Listen to him. He's even quoted Lucan's poem, or was it Virgil?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: It is most likely Virgil. He has quoted him below, "Fortune favors the bold."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: The quote about remembering things, how do you say it in Latin again? Forsan ... haec ... and then what? Hmm ...

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: The "et" is missing, Eberhard.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "And perhaps it will please us one day to remember these things."

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Yes, that's it! Hah. That old fart ... He cheated. These aren't even his words.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: What a fool. He doesn't know what he's talking about.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Heh ...
After a bitter laugh, both are silent for a moment.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Paul, I'll never be "pleased" looking back on any of this.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: If I have children one day, how will I tell them about all this?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I sent our fellow countrymen directly into the line of fire—a death trap—knowing full well that the enemy would retake the ground in mere hours.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Young lives, lost one after another, and for what? Some senseless orders?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I've heard enough. Put the letter away.
Paul slowly folds up the letter. Eberhard, however, snatches up the letterhead, crumples it into a ball, and throws it into the weeds beside the monument.
There is no more fighting, and for the first time in a long time, the day passes without the thunder of artillery.
The sunlight falls on blades of grass, tombstones, and birds in the air. Their songs finally can be heard once more.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: This feeling ... I've never felt it before. It's as though, for this one moment, I can—no, I have already taken control of my future.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Haheh. I'd forgotten how good it feels to be alive. Heh. For the first time in a very long while, my heart feels light, my friend.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: The choices I've made may be irreversible, but I've made up my mind. There is only one path for me now.
He looks to the top of the hill and starts climbing.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Do you not wish to continue your studies? Your writings are surely safely stored in the school's archives.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Would you return to school, Paul?

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: It is unlikely, but you still may.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: For what? For knowledge? A diploma? That might've mattered to the old me.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: But I'm no longer that boy.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Eberhard—

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: It's too late, my friend. Far too late.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I need some time alone. Please write the reply to Mr. Mühlenberge for both of us.
The weather is unseasonably mild, and Eberhard begins to climb the hill like a student on a field trip.
The sunshine and brisk air make the world feel new.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: The war is over, Paul. The sky is so blue.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: Just as it always was.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Just as it always was, hmm. Well said. Farewell, my friend!
He waves, turns, and walks away.
Paul stands and opens his notebook.

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "Dear Mr. Mühlenberge, your letter has been well received by your students."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "They have endured the darkest and hardest of times together. But now, the sorrow and pain have reached their end."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "They showed courage and loyalty, yet these virtues became a burden—one far too heavy for their young shoulders to bear."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "Therefore, I will not pile any more empty words upon them."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "War has shaped these young men into something else entirely. The knowledge you imparted is of no use to them now, nor will they ever again hear your teachings."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "At this time, I must inform you with the heaviest of hearts that ..."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "All of your students from Class 3 have fallen."

items.speaker: Paul
items.text: "With best regards. A dead man."
This concludes the records of the soldier Paul Haumann.
